value.rationale: The 2024 sharp finite-field parabola inequality identifies the optimal sixth moment but not the exact local spectral cost of departures from its extremizers. Resolving the q-dependent transverse Hessian pinpoints the least-stable phase directions, proves local nondegeneracy, and gives the sharp local stability coefficient for every prime power characteristic >=5. This is a natural stability invariant of a known sharp extension theorem, with nontrivial character-sum and finite-field symmetry input; the domain is the complete complementary characteristic range to a known characteristic-three analogue.
